title: Live Visitor Counts Were Inflated 10x — Now They're Real | vitalii.no
description:
My homepage badge claimed to show real-time visitors — but some historical days were quietly inflated by up to 10x, and I only found out by reading my own sync code.

Problem: I wanted a live badge showing visitors right now, today, this week and this month, without ever exposing my Cloudflare Analytics token to the browser or hammering the GraphQL API on every page load. Worse, the historical numbers I already had were wrong.

How it works: A Cloudflare Worker deployed at the edge queries the Web Analytics GraphQL API for four time windows, keeps the token in its own secret store, and caches each response for 60 seconds per colo with CORS headers so the frontend can call it directly. The React badge polls that endpoint once a minute in English, Norwegian and Ukrainian. Separately, a Python sync script's double-counting of Cloudflare's already-extrapolated sampling fields was found and fixed.

Result: The badge now refreshes every 60 seconds straight from the edge, and every historical day that had been multiplied by up to 10x has been corrected in a full backfill.
